descriptionSet.display: Al Jalali Fort, also known as Qal‘at al Jalālī, is the eastern of the two impressive defensive installations overlooking Muscat bay. The fort, along with al Mirani Fort (Qal‘at al Mīrānī) on the western edge of the bay, was built by the Portuguese, between 1586 -1588 CE on pre-existing foundations – possibly of native Omani or Hormuzi origin, its construction followed the second Ottoman attack on Muscat in 1582 CE. The fort strategically sits on a rocky outcrop in order to guard the bay, thus reinforcing the natural protection afforded by the topographic configuration of the town against both sea and land attacks. The fort consists of a fortified boundary wall, surrounding small garrison buildings, a watch tower and a large gun platform overlooking the bay, equipped with six iron and six bronze cannons, and a cistern cut into the rock. Around 1633 CE, the Portuguese Viceroy of India, Dom Miguell de Noronha, ordered the construction of additional fortifications and the location of the residence of the Muscat garrison and the ammunitions stores be accommodated in Al Jalali Fort. Throughout much of the twentieth century Al Jalali Fort continued as the country’s main prison.

description.source: Diwan of Royal Court Sultanate of Oman, Muscat Gate Museum: Memoirs of History, Muscat: Allegro Communications, 2001
